title: Sum of Nodes with Even-Valued Grandparent
interviewTips: State the brute-force approach first before presenting the optimal Arrays & Hashing technique.
Discuss Time and Space complexities upfront before writing code.
Test on empty inputs and single-element edge cases.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Recursive Formulation (Brute Force)
approaches.intuition: Break the problem down into overlapping subproblems. For each choice at the current state, branch recursively into smaller subproblems.
approaches.theory: Without memoization, overlapping subproblems are re-evaluated exponentially, resulting in an O(2^N) or O(K^N) recursion tree.

timeComplexity.explanation: Exponential branching recursion tree without memoization.

edgeCases: Base cases at n = 0 and n = 1.

approaches.name: Approach 2: Dynamic Programming (Bottom-Up Tabulation)
approaches.intuition: Identify the optimal substructure and dependency direction. Build a DP table starting from the base cases to avoid redundant recalculation.
approaches.theory: DP table satisfies optimal substructure: each state `dp[i]` is computed from previously solved subproblems in O(1) or O(K) transitions.

timeComplexity.explanation: Computes each table entry once with constant transitions.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Can often be space-optimized by storing only the previous state.

edgeCases: Empty input, negative inputs, large numbers requiring long long.
